Setting the local IP in "Add server" > "Connect to server" that is 192.168.0.2:8096 fails with
![image](https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin/assets/140865/885598c6-c121-41ea-942b-51eced3eebb7)

with 10.3.3.2:8096 jellyfin-web spin trying to connect, until I get the same error. With 192.168.0.2 the error was instantaneous.

Mind you have to set the internal LAN IPv4 IP as jellyfin-server IP in the jellyfin-web interface. This as you can connect to the jellyfin-web server from oustide with the external IPv4 IP but jellyfin-web will then connect to the jellyfin-server from inside the internal LAN. Thus you cannot tell jellyfin-web to connect to jellyfin-server with the external IPv4 IP from inside the LAN (except if your router support NAT loopboack https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Network_address_translation#NAT_hairpinning).

> "Change Listen Local Network Address to 0.0.0.0 WireGuard will work" means that you can add a server to the web, but this will not add a server through the device's IPv6 public network address.
After setting this option to empty (default is empty) the device's IPv6 public network adds servers normally, but through (public->nat->10.3.3.1)->WireGuard->(10.3.3.2->nat to local address->jellfin) the server cannot be added from the web, and the web can be accessed normally.

by "change Listen Local Network Address to 0.0.0.0 WireGuard will work", what setting did you change (AllowedIPs in wireguard peer config?)? If so indeed you have to allow both an IPv4 range and an IPv6 range (you can add more than one range in AllowedIPs.
https://github.com/pirate/wireguard-docs#allowedips (the full IPv6 range is `::/0`.

by "you can add a server to the web, but this will not add a server through the device's IPv6 public network address.", you mean you can add a "jellyfin server" in the jellyfin-web "Connect server" field by IPv4 IP?


> > The main problem is that the web can be opened, but the server cannot be added from the web.
> It is normal to use local address in local network, and definitely use public address outside. I have only one device with public IPv4 and I use WireGuard to connect the two networks.

Agreed. I was just being explicit the IPv4 IP you use to connect to jellyfin-web can both be internal and external IP, while the IP you set in jellyfin-web to access jellyfin-server to me should be the internal IPv4 IP (as I believe jellyfin-web is a web server thus access jellyfin-server from inside the LAN).



And indeed IPv6: http://lroute.315490.xyz:8096/ does not even ask for a server and prompt for a user as in my setup (even though my setup is IPv4, also behind wireguard).
I use an image based on the jellyfin/jellyfin arm64 docker image with ID 132ebc382c5a (`docker images`). I use a locally modified ffmpeg package to which I added a few patches to test video acceleration on rockchip ARM.


Your jellyfin server ip setup (the `ip a` output from a console) might help too as the error you get from jellyfin is about Network.MatchesExternalInterface. There is probably a jellyfin bug in that the could code handle the error gracefully and show an error to the user. Still something out of the ordinary triggers this bug and might get away with it by tweaking your openwrt setup.

> You can't connect using the private network address (192.168.0.2) without being in my local network.

This I am not confident about. I mean I cannot connect to jellyfin-web via 192.168.0.2. But I can connect to jellyfin-web via its external IPv4 IP and ask jellyfin-web to connect to 192.168.0.2 or even 127.0.0.1 (I believe jellyfin-web connect directly on its box to the jellyfin-server)
This is why I was telling to set 192.168.0.2 or 10.3.3.2 in "Add server" of jellyfin-web.
But if you have NAT loopback even with your external IP the connection should work.

> And the address 10.3.3.2 should not be accessible by the external network because it is the address defined inside the WireGuard tunnel and you are not connected to the tunnel.

That I did not pay attention to. That is true that you are the only one who can test with this IPv4 IP. What happens if you reach the jellyfin-web via 10.3.3.2 from your browser from a box that is connected to the wireguard VPN?


I took a look at the code (I am not a jellyfin developer), just asking you about details that could help sort out why jellyfin fails (or find a workaround what in the setup jellyfin does not play well with).

Emby.Server.Implementations.ApplicationHost.GetPublicSystemInfo(HttpRequest request) https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin/blob/master/Emby.Server.Implementations/ApplicationHost.cs#L983
Emby.Server.Implementations.ApplicationHost.GetSmartApiUrl(HttpRequest request) https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin/blob/master/Emby.Server.Implementations/ApplicationHost.cs#L1017
Emby.Server.Implementations.ApplicationHost.GetSmartApiUrl(IPAddress remoteAddr) https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin/blob/master/Emby.Server.Implementations/ApplicationHost.cs#L998

from these lines the NetManager.GetBindInterface IP the jellyfin error is about is parsed from the http request URL.

(...)
Jellyfin.Networking.Manager.NetworkManager.GetBindInterface(IPObject source, Nullable`1& port) https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin/blob/master/Jellyfin.Networking/Manager/NetworkManager.cs#L391
Jellyfin.Networking.Manager.NetworkManager.MatchesExternalInterface(IPObject source, String& result) https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin/blob/master/Jellyfin.Networking/Manager/NetworkManager.cs#L391

http://<redacted-host>:8096/ , this URL points to 120.35.133.25, which is not on any interface that jellyfin can list on its box.
So the jellyfin error you have could be that it does not play well when the IP it is reached from is not on the interfaces available on the jellyfin box.

But it could well be this setup is not even what you want. A reverse proxy could be the correct answer for reaching jellyfin via a gateway public IPv4 http://<redacted-host>:8096/ (I believe 120.35.133.25 is not the external IPv4 IP of the openwrt router but another box).
Or you could do as I do and access your jellyfin server via its wireguard IPv4 IP 10.3.3.2, or even via wireguard to the internal IPv4 IP 192.168.0.2 if you set ad this range in the AllowedIPs for this peer.
I am not confident from the discussion we had you want external IPv4 IP access to this jellyfin server out of the wireguard VPN.

> After setting the LAN network options it works fine, I am accessing a public device and then accessing another LAN jellyfin through a WireGuard tunnel on this public device

If you want to access jellyfin though the wireguard tunnel you should access it with 10.3.3.2.
Could you confirm that jellyfin works properly if you type http://10.3.3.2:8096 on your wireguard client?


> root@OpenWrt_PVE:~# echo $(curl http://127.0.0.1:8096/System/Info/Public)
this only means that you can access jellyfin on 127.0.0.1 from the openwrt jellyfin box only. This is the way 127.0.01 works, ie 127.0.0.1 only works to access the box you are on not other boxes. So from the CDN you cannot use 127.0.0.1 to access your jellyfin server.

If you open an ssh tunnel you redirect a local port on the box you are on to another local port on the remote box. Thus 127.0.0.1:<your local port> will forward traffic to other_box:other_port. 

Out of opening an ssh tunnel from your local box 8096 port to the jellyfin box 8096 port, 127.0.0.1:8096 only allow you to access a jellyfin instance local to the box your browser runs on.

> But this is forwarding access to https://jellyfin.315490.xyz/ to port 8096 on OpenWrt

can you explain what do you  mean? how is jellyfin.315490.xyz redirecting traffic to openwrt port 8096?

Mind we are polluting the bug tracker, the only jellyfin issue I see is that if you access jellyfin via an IPv4 IP that is not defined on an interface on the box jellyfin runs on, jellyfin throw an exception.
